mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in all market regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% indicates a tightening labor market, which signals strong economic growth and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 3.5, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5.0%, the market anticipates aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery (HOUST > 1500 thousand units), the S&P 500 tends to rise over the next 60 days as housing strength drives broader economic expansion and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: During periods when HOUST > 1500, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in reduced corporate activity.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% for three consecutive months triggers expectations of higher interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL has been above 3.5% for 3 consecutive months, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When private payrolls (PAYEMS) exceed 150,000 and retail sales (RSAFS) surpass 650,000 million dollars, the economy is in a strong expansion phase, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 150000 and RSAFS > 650000, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), the S&P 500 typically rises over the next 60 days due to sustained consumer spending and corporate profit growth supported by a tight labor market.
failure_condition: During periods when UNRATE < 3.5%, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
